solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Splendid large university Fred now recalled

indicators.note: recalled in the sense of called back, so the words Fred now are read from the end

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man called Fred remembers something splendid about a big university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reads the name and the word after it backwards, so 'Fred now' is fodder rather than a person and a moment; the university and large letters then follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives of high praise, marvellous or excellent.

clue.text: Gradually impair dress in blue

parts.note: to wear clothes is to be dressed in them
feeling blue means feeling down, depressed

explanation.surface: Wearing a blue outfit slowly spoils it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear something down is to erode or weaken it bit by bit.

clue.text: Egg container upside-down

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upside-down reads the word for the container from the bottom up

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: An egg box has been turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse.

clue.text: Go beyond former prison room briefly

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word for a prison room cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a cell is a room in a prison

explanation.surface: Someone moves on from a former prison cell after a short stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass or outdo, going beyond others.

clue.text: Dressing European celebrity in something dirty

parts.note: the French are Europeans

indicators.note: in places the word for celebrity within the word for something dirty

parts.note: mud is dirt
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous European is caught wearing filthy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: French mustard is a condiment, and dressing here means a sauce or condiment for food.

clue.text: Greek character welcomes a dance

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the Greek letter holds the A inside it

parts.note: lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person greets someone with a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian partner dance popular in 1989.

clue.text: Criticise cooking equipment

definitions.meaning: to ... a show is to review it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the kitchen kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan is both a verb for slating something and a noun for a saucepan.

clue.text: Gift disheartened lady at once

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters of lady are dropped, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: A woman is saddened by a gift straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves the outer letters of lady, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage presently meant immediately, without delay, as well as soon.

clue.text: Snow fell endlessly — at this festive time?

indicators.note: endlessly drops the first and last letter from each of the two words snow and fell

explanation.surface: Snow came down at Christmas, as people hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips SNOW to NO and FELL to EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for Christmas, the festive season.

clue.text: Creative work left in reserve, writing for newspaper?

parts.note: art is creative work

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for left within the word for reserve

parts.note: ice means reserve, a cool formality of manner

explanation.surface: A creative piece is held back, perhaps pieces written for a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a piece of journalism printed in a newspaper.

clue.text: Organ belonging to me? That's not true

parts.note: my means belonging to me
the eye is an organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a body part is theirs, and is told it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: My eye is an old exclamation dismissing a claim as nonsense.

clue.text: Remain healthy after fourth grade

indicators.note: after puts the word for healthy following the grade letter

parts.note: grades run A, B, C, D, so the fourth is D
well means healthy

explanation.surface: A pupil stays fit after reaching fourth grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to stay or reside somewhere.

clue.text: Wife leaves old English Duke for jazzy American one?

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the letter for wife is taken out of the duke's name

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington was the English general who won at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A wife abandons an English aristocrat for a flashier American.
explanation.walkthrough: The jazzy American is another Duke: Duke Ellington, the bandleader; the question mark flags the second Duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was a celebrated American jazz composer and bandleader.

clue.text: In court, earl turned red

indicators.note: in places the rearranged earl within the abbreviation for court
turned means twisted round into a new order, so the letters of earl are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman blushes at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is a red Bordeaux wine, and also the colour named after it.

clue.text: Lazy boozer claims state benefit over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
claims means takes hold of, so the word for pub holds the benefit inside it

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn
the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: An idle drinker lives on benefits for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent describes someone idle, avoiding effort.

clue.text: Bill originally contained different tax on printer

parts.note: Bill is a short form of the name William

indicators.note: originally takes only the opening letter of contained
different signals the letters of tax on rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill came with a fresh tax on a printing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' makes AXTON from TAX ON. William Caxton set up England's first printing press in the 1470s.
explanation.definitionFit: Caxton was the first English printer, bringing the press to England.

clue.text: Copy current computer technology in China

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in puts the computer letters inside the word for friend

parts.note: china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: Up-to-date Chinese computing copies others.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china is a friend, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy or mimic.

clue.text: Granite-like rock in Dordogne is spectacular

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words Dordogne is spectacular

explanation.surface: Rocks in the Dordogne region of France look spectacular.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse banded metamorphic rock often resembling granite.

clue.text: Unknown among elite soldiers with zero authority

indicators.note: among puts the unknown letter amid the soldiers' initials

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
Y is an algebraic unknown
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An outsider among special forces has no authority at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so means the power to decide, permission or authority.

clue.text: Physical strength is back, regenerated

indicators.note: back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: something regenerated is made new

explanation.surface: Muscle power has returned after renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew, a tendon, stands by extension for muscular power.

clue.text: Golf competition half-seen after work

indicators.note: after puts the half word following the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: half takes two of the four letters of seen, here its second pair

explanation.surface: A golf tournament half watched after the day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open is golf's oldest major championship.

clue.text: Father accepts one dry type of bread

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the word for father holds the other letters

parts.note: pa is father
I is the Roman numeral for one
TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking

explanation.surface: Dad takes a single dry piece of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread.

clue.text: Racecourse area popular with elder, for example

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
the elder is a tree

explanation.surface: An older person likes a spot near a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree, near Liverpool, hosts the Grand National horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous English horse-racing course.

clue.text: Draymen regularly avoided Sussex town

indicators.note: skipping every other letter of Draymen, avoiding the odd ones, leaves the even letters

explanation.surface: Brewery delivery men steered clear of a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a historic small town in East Sussex, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is an old harbour town in the English county of East Sussex.

clue.text: Knight meets a French religious lady

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A knight meets a French woman of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order.

clue.text: Type of mortgage Mo and Ned went to arrange

indicators.note: to arrange means to put in order, so the letters of Mo, Ned and went are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple go to sort out their home loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' shuffles MONEDWENT; 'and' only joins the names.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment mortgage is a home loan repaid by an investment policy.
